title: RAID
description: Documented public storage redundancy (Patterson, Gibson, Katz (1987)) for the Fault-Tolerance Architect capability area.
body:
RAID is a documented storage redundancy from Patterson, Gibson, Katz (1987). Redundant Arrays of Inexpensive Disks: the foundational technique surviving disk failures via parity and mirroring.

How it works: It works by injecting faults over many trials, measuring which recover and the median recovery time.

Documented uses of this capability area include supercomputer job scheduling, cryptographic migration planning, chaos-engineering programs, and disaster-recovery verification.

title: Raft consensus
description: Documented public fault-tolerant coordination (Ongaro & Ousterhout) for the Fault-Tolerance Architect capability area.
body:
Raft consensus is a documented fault-tolerant coordination from Ongaro & Ousterhout. Leader-election consensus letting services survive node failures without split-brain — the standard coordination primitive.

How it works: It works by simulating a randomized leader election: each node votes for a random candidate and a majority elects the leader.
